Fixes #7710, #7690 

A bug was introduced in https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/pull/7141#discussion_r503800703 that changes the loading of pre-trained special tokens files. This PR more or less reverts the critical changes so that RAG works again. This can be verified by running this test:

```
RUN_SLOW=1 pytest tests/test_modeling_rag.py::RagModelIntegrationTests::test_rag_sequence_generate_batch
```

A new RAG tokenizer test was added.

issue_context.title: 2 RAG test failures
issue_context.body:
The two failures here look related to recent tokenizer changes:

https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/runs/1236753957?check_suite_focus=true

```
=========================== short test summary info ============================

FAILED tests/test_modeling_rag.py::RagModelIntegrationTests::test_rag_sequence_generate_batch
FAILED tests/test_modeling_rag.py::RagModelIntegrationTests::test_rag_token_generate_batch
```
comments:
@sshleifer - thanks a lot for the issue! 

This error seems related to https://github.com/huggingface/transformers/issues/7690#issuecomment-707382445.

review_comments:
The difference between the old (and proposed here) method and the new method (leveraging `convert_added_token`) is that the one leveraging `convert_added_token` manages an unlimited level of nesting as it's recursive, @thomwolf?

Isn't it possible to still leverage the `convert_added_token` method?

I could write a new recursive `convert_added_token` function. But the one used previously does not seem to work for RAG. The line: `if isinstance(obj, dict) and "__type" in obj and obj["__type"] == "AddedToken":` does not seem to fit for RAG's tokenizer `facebook/rag-token-nq`. 

Also not sure if the `special_token_map` would ever have more than 2 levels of nesting, but @LysandreJik @thomwolf @n1t0 probably know better here!

I see indeed. We need to update the `save_pretrained` method as well then.

The previous behavior of considering all dict objects as `AddedToken` seemed a bit fragile to me.
I'll update this a little bit if you don't mind, probably we can just check that all the keys in the dict are in the fields of the AddedToken class before converting it.
